scope: Selected medication references, not an exhaustive drug catalog, complete monographs, a treatment recommendation, or a prescription. Verify the complete current label and patient-specific factors. FDA status refers to the stated US product, indication and age group.

sertraline.name: Sertraline
sertraline.sideEffects: Nausea, diarrhea, sweating, tremor, sexual dysfunction.
sertraline.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; pimozide; MAOI use or within 14 days (includes linezolid/IV methylene blue).
sertraline.cautions: Suicidality warning in younger patients; review hepatic impairment and serotonergic/bleeding interactions.
sertraline.labs: No routine serum drug level. Consider sodium with hyponatremia risk or symptoms; other labs follow the clinical assessment.
sertraline.monitoring: Monitor mood/suicidality, activation/mania, serotonin toxicity, bleeding, and discontinuation effects.

escitalopram.name: Escitalopram
escitalopram.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to escitalopram/citalopram; MAOI restrictions including linezolid/IV methylene blue.
escitalopram.cautions: Review QT risk, hepatic/older-adult dosing and suicidality warning.
escitalopram.labs: No routine serum drug level. Consider sodium with hyponatremia risk or symptoms; other labs follow the clinical assessment.
escitalopram.monitoring: Monitor mood/suicidality, activation/mania, serotonin toxicity, bleeding, and discontinuation effects.

fluoxetine.name: Fluoxetine (Prozac)
fluoxetine.sideEffects: Nausea, insomnia, anxiety, reduced appetite, sexual dysfunction.
fluoxetine.contraindications: MAOIs: wait at least 14 days after an MAOI and at least 5 weeks after fluoxetine before an MAOI; pimozide; thioridazine (including 5-week washout).
fluoxetine.cautions: Long half-life; CYP2D6 interactions, QT risk and suicidality warning. Do not use antidepressant monotherapy for bipolar I depression.
fluoxetine.labs: No routine serum drug level. Consider sodium with hyponatremia risk or symptoms; other labs follow the clinical assessment.
fluoxetine.monitoring: Monitor mood/suicidality, activation/mania, serotonin toxicity, bleeding, and discontinuation effects.

venlafaxine.name: Venlafaxine XR
venlafaxine.sideEffects: Nausea, sweating, insomnia, sexual dysfunction, constipation.
venlafaxine.cautions: Suicidality warning; dose reductions for renal/hepatic impairment; gradual discontinuation.
venlafaxine.labs: No routine serum drug level. Consider sodium with hyponatremia risk or symptoms; other labs follow the clinical assessment. Consider lipids during long-term therapy.
venlafaxine.monitoring: Monitor BP/pulse as well as mood, activation and discontinuation symptoms.

buspirone.name: Buspirone
buspirone.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; MAOI restrictions including linezolid/IV methylene blue.
buspirone.cautions: Not a rescue drug. Review CYP3A4 interactions; severe renal/hepatic impairment: use not recommended.
buspirone.labs: No routine serum level or universal lab panel; assess renal/hepatic function when indicated.
buspirone.monitoring: Review dizziness, serotonin toxicity, response and adherence.

lithium.name: Lithium carbonate
lithium.contraindications: Linked product: hypersensitivity to an inactive ingredient.
lithium.cautions: Narrow therapeutic index; avoid severe renal impairment, dehydration and sodium depletion. NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics can raise levels; review pregnancy risk.
lithium.labs: Baseline renal function, electrolytes, thyroid, calcium and pregnancy status when applicable. Obtain a 12-hour trough after 3 days per label, after changes, and regularly; repeat renal/thyroid/calcium monitoring.
lithium.monitoring: Track hydration, tremor, GI/neurologic toxicity and interacting medicines. Serum concentrations guide dosing, not pill strength.

lamotrigine.name: Lamotrigine
lamotrigine.cautions: Serious rash/SJS/TEN warning: assess new rash urgently; stop unless clearly unrelated. Valproate, enzyme inducers and estrogen change dosing; restart after interruption may require retitration. Not an acute-mania treatment.
lamotrigine.labs: No established routine therapeutic serum target. Renal/hepatic assessment and CBC/LFTs when clinically indicated (e.g., systemic hypersensitivity).
lamotrigine.monitoring: Assess rash, fever/systemic symptoms, suicidality and cardiac disease risk. Never accelerate the titration.

quetiapine.name: Quetiapine IR
quetiapine.sideEffects: Sedation, dry mouth, dizziness, constipation, weight gain.
quetiapine.cautions: Review metabolic effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and tardive dyskinesia. Boxed warning: increased mortality in older adults with dementia-related psychosis. CYP3A4 interactions and hepatic impairment require adjustments.
quetiapine.labs: Baseline and follow-up glucose or HbA1c and lipids; CBC if prior low WBC/drug-related neutropenia. Additional tests are risk/symptom-directed.
quetiapine.monitoring: Track weight/BMI, BP, orthostasis, movement symptoms/AIMS, and treatment response. ECG when cardiac/QT risk warrants.

aripiprazole.name: Aripiprazole
aripiprazole.cautions: Review metabolic effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and tardive dyskinesia. Boxed warning: increased mortality in older adults with dementia-related psychosis. Review impulse-control problems and CYP2D6/CYP3A4 adjustments.
aripiprazole.labs: Baseline and follow-up glucose or HbA1c and lipids; CBC if prior low WBC/drug-related neutropenia. Additional tests are risk/symptom-directed.
aripiprazole.monitoring: Track weight/BMI, BP, orthostasis, movement symptoms/AIMS, and treatment response. ECG when cardiac/QT risk warrants. Assess compulsive behaviors.

risperidone.name: Risperidone
risperidone.sideEffects: Sedation, EPS, weight gain, prolactin-related effects.
risperidone.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to risperidone, paliperidone or ingredients.
risperidone.cautions: Review metabolic effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and tardive dyskinesia. Boxed warning: increased mortality in older adults with dementia-related psychosis. Renal/hepatic impairment requires lower doses.
risperidone.labs: Baseline and follow-up glucose or HbA1c and lipids; CBC if prior low WBC/drug-related neutropenia. Additional tests are risk/symptom-directed. Check prolactin when symptoms or clinical risk warrant.
risperidone.monitoring: Track weight/BMI, BP, orthostasis, movement symptoms/AIMS, and treatment response. ECG when cardiac/QT risk warrants.

paliperidone.name: Paliperidone ER
paliperidone.sideEffects: EPS, akathisia, tachycardia, somnolence, prolactin effects.
paliperidone.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to paliperidone, risperidone or ingredients.
paliperidone.cautions: Review metabolic effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and tardive dyskinesia. Boxed warning: increased mortality in older adults with dementia-related psychosis. Renal dosing and QT risk require review; swallow whole.
paliperidone.labs: Baseline and follow-up glucose or HbA1c and lipids; CBC if prior low WBC/drug-related neutropenia. Additional tests are risk/symptom-directed. Check renal function for dosing; prolactin if clinically indicated.
paliperidone.monitoring: Track weight/BMI, BP, orthostasis, movement symptoms/AIMS, and treatment response. ECG when cardiac/QT risk warrants.

concerta.name: Methylphenidate ER (Concerta)
concerta.sideEffects: Appetite loss, insomnia, anxiety, headache, weight loss.
concerta.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; concomitant MAOI or within 14 days.
concerta.cautions: Boxed warning: abuse, misuse and addiction. Avoid serious cardiac disease; review glaucoma, tics and mania/psychosis risk. Swallow whole; other methylphenidate formulations are not interchangeable.
concerta.labs: No universal routine lab panel. Obtain tests for specific history/examination concerns; ECG/cardiology assessment when indicated.
concerta.monitoring: Check BP/pulse, weight/appetite, sleep, mood/psychosis and misuse risk. Pediatric use also requires growth monitoring.

lisdexamfetamine.name: Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse)
lisdexamfetamine.strengths: Capsules 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 mg; chewables 10–60 mg in 10-mg steps
lisdexamfetamine.sideEffects: Dry mouth, appetite loss, insomnia, anxiety, increased pulse.
lisdexamfetamine.contraindications: Amphetamine/product hypersensitivity; MAOI use or within 14 days.
lisdexamfetamine.cautions: Boxed warning: abuse, misuse and addiction. Avoid serious cardiac disease; assess mania/psychosis and serotonin toxicity risk. Renal limits apply; not for weight loss.
lisdexamfetamine.labs: No universal routine lab panel. Obtain tests for specific history/examination concerns; ECG/cardiology assessment when indicated.
lisdexamfetamine.monitoring: Check BP/pulse, weight/appetite, sleep, mood/psychosis and misuse risk. Pediatric use also requires growth monitoring.

atomoxetine.name: Atomoxetine
atomoxetine.sideEffects: Nausea, dry mouth, appetite loss, constipation, sexual/urinary effects.
atomoxetine.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; MAOIs within 14 days; narrow-angle glaucoma; pheochromocytoma; severe cardiovascular disorders.
atomoxetine.cautions: Pediatric suicidality warning; rare severe liver injury. Hepatic impairment/CYP2D6 inhibitors or poor metabolism change dosing.
atomoxetine.labs: Liver tests if jaundice or liver-injury symptoms; routine lab testing is not universally required.
atomoxetine.monitoring: Monitor BP/pulse, weight, mood/suicidality and urinary symptoms.

clonidine-er.name: Clonidine ER
clonidine-er.sideEffects: Somnolence, fatigue, dry mouth, constipation, dizziness.
clonidine-er.cautions: Hypotension/bradycardia; taper to prevent rebound hypertension. Swallow whole; do not substitute immediate release mg-for-mg.
clonidine-er.labs: No universal routine labs; renal function if impairment is suspected.
clonidine-er.monitoring: BP/pulse before starting, after increases and periodically; assess sedation/syncope.

doxepin.name: Low-dose doxepin (Silenor)
doxepin.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; MAOIs within 14 days; untreated narrow-angle glaucoma or severe urinary retention.
doxepin.cautions: Avoid alcohol/CNS depressants; ordinarily not recommended in severe sleep apnea. These doses are not antidepressant-dose doxepin.
doxepin.labs: No routine serum level or universal lab panel.
doxepin.monitoring: Assess next-day sedation, abnormal sleep behaviors, mood and persistent insomnia.

ramelteon.name: Ramelteon
ramelteon.contraindications: Prior ramelteon-associated angioedema; do not combine with fluvoxamine.
ramelteon.cautions: Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment or severe sleep apnea; review CNS depressants.
ramelteon.labs: No universal routine labs. Prolactin/testosterone assessment for relevant reproductive/endocrine symptoms.
ramelteon.monitoring: Assess next-day impairment, abnormal behaviors and response.

modafinil.name: Modafinil
modafinil.cautions: Serious rash; psychiatric/cardiovascular effects; reduces steroidal contraceptive effectiveness during use and for 1 month after. For OSA, does not treat the obstruction.
modafinil.labs: No universal routine labs; hepatic assessment when indicated (severe impairment: half dose).
modafinil.monitoring: Track BP/pulse, psychiatric symptoms, rash, sleepiness and adherence to primary OSA therapy.

gabapentin-enacarbil.name: Gabapentin enacarbil (Horizant)
gabapentin-enacarbil.contraindications: None listed in linked label; this does not mean risk-free.
gabapentin-enacarbil.cautions: Respiratory depression with CNS depressants/respiratory disease; suicidality; renal adjustment. Not interchangeable with gabapentin.
gabapentin-enacarbil.labs: Renal function for dosing; RLS assessment: ferritin and iron/TIBC-derived transferrin saturation.
gabapentin-enacarbil.monitoring: Assess sedation, breathing, driving impairment and mood.

mdd.note: Compare monotherapy options by prior response, comorbidities and patient preference. Augmentation/TRD options are not comprehensively covered.

options.dose: Start 50 mg orally daily; increase 25–50 mg no more often than weekly if needed; range 50–200 mg/day.
10 mg orally daily; maximum 20 mg/day. Adults: wait at least 1 week before an increase; older adults/hepatic impairment: recommended 10 mg/day.
Start 20 mg orally each morning; increase only after several weeks if needed; maximum 80 mg/day.
Start 37.5–75 mg orally daily with food; usual target 75 mg/day, maximum 225 mg/day; use label-specific titration.

pdd.note: Psychotherapy and medication may be used; dose references below are extrapolated from adult MDD, not a separate labeled PDD regimen.

options.dose: Start 50 mg orally daily; increase 25–50 mg no more often than weekly if needed; range 50–200 mg/day.
options.notes: MDD dose reference; establish the depressive syndrome and individualize.

options.dose: 10 mg orally daily; maximum 20 mg/day. Adults: wait at least 1 week before an increase; older adults/hepatic impairment: recommended 10 mg/day.
options.notes: MDD dose reference; no diagnosis-specific approved regimen shown.

bipolar-i.note: Select by episode phase. Antidepressant monotherapy is not an appropriate default for bipolar I depression.

options.dose: Label start 300 mg orally three times/day; adjust using 12-hour troughs. Label goals: acute 0.8–1.2 mEq/L; maintenance 0.8–1.0 mEq/L. Lower individualized starts may be needed.
Without valproate or glucuronidation inducers: weeks 1–2, 25 mg/day; 3–4, 50 mg/day; week 5, 100 mg/day; week 6+, 200 mg/day. Other regimens require a different label schedule.
IR bedtime schedule: day 1, 50 mg; day 2, 100 mg; day 3, 200 mg; day 4+, 300 mg/day. Adjust for tolerability/hepatic impairment.
Start 50 mg orally twice/day; label escalation to 400 mg/day by day 4; range 400–800 mg/day; maximum 800 mg/day.

bipolar-ii.note: Avoid treating hypomania and bipolar depression as the same medication phase. Maintenance choices need separate review.

options.dose: IR bedtime schedule: day 1, 50 mg; day 2, 100 mg; day 3, 200 mg; day 4+, 300 mg/day. Adjust for tolerability/hepatic impairment.

cyclothymia.note: No FDA-approved cyclothymia-specific medication. Mood-stabilizer use is off-label and evidence is limited; no standardized cyclothymia dose is supplied.

gad.note: Consider CBT and medication according to severity and preference.

options.dose: 10 mg orally daily; maximum 20 mg/day. Adults: wait at least 1 week before an increase; older adults/hepatic impairment: recommended 10 mg/day.
Start 37.5–75 mg orally daily with food; usual target 75 mg/day, maximum 225 mg/day; use label-specific titration.
Start 7.5 mg orally twice/day; increase total daily dose by 5 mg every 2–3 days if needed; common total 20–30 mg/day divided; maximum 60 mg/day. Take consistently with or without food.

panic.note: CBT is an option; start antidepressants cautiously and reassess activation.

options.dose: Start 25 mg orally daily; increase 25–50 mg no more often than weekly; range 50–200 mg/day.
Start 10 mg orally daily; after 1 week increase to 20 mg/day; studied range 10–60 mg/day.
Start 37.5 mg orally daily for 7 days, then 75 mg/day; maximum 225 mg/day; later increases at intervals of at least 7 days.
Start 25 mg orally daily; increase 25–50 mg no more often than weekly; range 50–200 mg/day.
75 mg orally once daily with food; higher doses have not shown additional benefit in the linked label.

phobia.note: Exposure-based treatment is central. No routine medication regimen for the core phobia is supplied; symptom-specific adjuncts require separate assessment.

separation.note: CBT and family/school work are important. SSRIs may be considered off-label for pediatric anxiety; age/weight-specific separation-anxiety doses are not yet in this catalog.

mutism.note: Behavioral, speech-language and school interventions are central. Off-label SSRI use needs specialist assessment; no selective-mutism dosing monograph is included.

ocd.note: Exposure and response prevention is an important treatment option. Adequate trials and augmentation require separate review.

options.dose: Adult start 50 mg orally daily; increase 25–50 mg no more often than weekly; maximum 200 mg/day.
Adult start 20 mg orally each morning; recommended 20–60 mg/day, maximum 80 mg/day; increases after several weeks if needed.
Age 6–12: start 25 mg orally daily; age 13–17: 50 mg daily; increase no more often than weekly; maximum 200 mg/day, accounting for lower body weight.

ptsd.note: Trauma-focused psychotherapy is preferred when feasible. This panel does not cover all symptom-targeted adjuncts.

options.dose: Start 25 mg orally daily; increase 25–50 mg no more often than weekly; range 50–200 mg/day.
VA/DoD reference range 75–300 mg/day orally; individualized initiation/titration. Above 225 mg/day exceeds the linked XR label maximum for its approved anxiety/depression indications.
options.notes: Off-label PTSD regimen; not the labeled MDD maximum.

schizophrenia.note: Selected oral options only. First-episode dosing, clozapine, long-acting injectables and treatment resistance require separate assessment.

options.dose: Start/target 10–15 mg orally daily; maximum 30 mg/day. Generally wait 2 weeks before increasing.
Start 2 mg/day orally; recommended 4–8 mg/day. Titrate individually; higher studied doses are not routine targets.
Start 25 mg orally twice daily; titrate per label to 150–750 mg/day in divided doses; maximum 750 mg/day for this IR label.
6 mg orally once daily; range 3–12 mg/day, maximum 12 mg/day; renal dosing differs. Swallow ER tablets whole.

schizophreniform.note: Antipsychotic treatment may be used off-label; duration and lower starting doses depend on first-episode tolerability and course. Doses below are schizophrenia-label references, not diagnosis-specific validated regimens.

options.dose: Start/target 10–15 mg orally daily; maximum 30 mg/day. Generally wait 2 weeks before increasing.
Start 2 mg/day orally; recommended 4–8 mg/day. Titrate individually; higher studied doses are not routine targets.

brief-psychosis.note: Antipsychotic treatment may be used off-label; duration and lower starting doses depend on first-episode tolerability and course. Doses below are schizophrenia-label references, not diagnosis-specific validated regimens.

options.dose: Start/target 10–15 mg orally daily; maximum 30 mg/day. Generally wait 2 weeks before increasing.
Start 2 mg/day orally; recommended 4–8 mg/day. Titrate individually; higher studied doses are not routine targets.

schizoaffective.note: Select treatment for both psychosis and the mood component; bipolar versus depressive type matters.

options.dose: 6 mg orally once daily; range 3–12 mg/day, maximum 12 mg/day; renal adjustments apply. Monotherapy or adjunctive use per label.

adhd.note: Selected formulations only. Assess cardiovascular history, misuse risk and coexisting conditions.

options.dose: Adults 18–65 new to methylphenidate: 18 or 36 mg orally each morning; increase 18 mg at weekly intervals; range 18–72 mg/day; swallow whole.
Start 30 mg orally each morning; increase by 10–20 mg at weekly intervals; range 30–70 mg/day, maximum 70 mg/day; renal limits apply.
Adults: 40 mg/day orally, target 80 mg/day after at least 3 days; if needed after another 2–4 weeks, maximum 100 mg/day. CYP2D6/hepatic factors require slower/lower dosing.

Start 0.1 mg orally at bedtime for 1 week; increase 0.1 mg/day at weekly intervals to at most 0.4 mg/day. Above 0.1 mg/day divide AM/bedtime with equal or larger bedtime portion. Taper by no more than 0.1 mg every 3–7 days.

autism.note: Medication does not treat the core features. The pediatric options below target clinically significant irritability associated with autism; psychosocial assessment and support remain central.

options.dose: Start 2 mg orally daily; increase to 5 mg/day, then 10 or 15 mg/day if needed at intervals of at least 1 week; recommended 5–15 mg/day.

Under 20 kg: start 0.25 mg/day; 20 kg or more: 0.5 mg/day orally. After at least 4 days target 0.5 or 1 mg/day respectively; hold at least 14 days before further label-guided increases. Range 0.5–3 mg/day; no data below 15 kg.

odd.note: Behavioral/parent interventions first. Treat coexisting ADHD or other conditions according to their own assessment; no routine ODD-specific medication regimen.

conduct.note: Psychosocial and parent interventions are central. Do not offer medication routinely for conduct problems; severe aggression may warrant short-term specialist treatment after psychosocial nonresponse.

dmdd.note: No FDA-approved DMDD-specific medication. Psychotherapy, parent support and treatment of comorbidities guide care; stimulants, antidepressants or atypical antipsychotics may be used off-label for selected targets, with specialist review.

anorexia.note: Nutritional rehabilitation, medical stabilization and eating-disorder therapy are central. Do not use medication as sole treatment. Off-label adjuncts/comorbidities require specialist review. Assess electrolytes, magnesium/phosphate and ECG based on malnutrition, purging and refeeding risk.

bulimia.note: Medication complements eating-disorder treatment. Review electrolytes and ECG risk with purging. Bupropion is contraindicated with current/prior bulimia or anorexia.

options.dose: 60 mg orally each morning; some patients require gradual titration to this dose.

bed.note: Psychotherapy remains important. The stimulant reference is for moderate-to-severe BED in adults and is not a weight-loss treatment.

options.dose: Start 30 mg orally each morning; increase by 20 mg at roughly weekly intervals; target 50–70 mg/day, maximum 70 mg/day. Stop if binge eating does not improve.

insomnia.note: CBT-I is first-line. Match sleep-onset versus sleep-maintenance problems; assess sleep apnea and other causes.

options.dose: Adults: 6 mg orally within 30 minutes of bedtime (3 mg may suit some); older adults start 3 mg; maximum 6 mg/day. Avoid within 3 hours of food.
8 mg orally within 30 minutes of bedtime; maximum 8 mg/day; avoid with or immediately after a high-fat meal.

circadian.note: Timing-directed light, schedule and sometimes melatonin depend on subtype. No universal melatonin dose/timing fits all circadian disorders. The option below applies only to diagnosed shift-work disorder with excessive sleepiness.

options.target: Excessive sleepiness associated with shift-work disorder
options.dose: 200 mg orally about 1 hour before the work shift. Not a general circadian phase-resetting treatment.

narcolepsy.note: Selected wake-promoting reference only. Cataplexy and other symptoms require sleep-specialist management; other approved treatments are not yet cataloged.

options.dose: 200 mg orally once each morning. Severe hepatic impairment: half the recommended dose.

osa.note: Treat the obstruction (e.g., PAP) first. This adjunct treats residual excessive sleepiness, not airway obstruction; confirm adequate primary treatment.

options.target: Residual excessive sleepiness associated with OSA
options.dose: 200 mg orally each morning; not a substitute for effective treatment of the obstruction.

rls.note: Assess iron status and aggravating medications/sleep apnea. Iron replacement and other alpha-2-delta ligands need separate clinical dosing review.

options.dose: 600 mg orally once daily around 5 PM with food; renal adjustment required. Swallow whole. Higher RLS doses add adverse effects without added benefit.
